ai_assistance: AI-assisted protocol drafting, runner implementation and validation; human operator reviews claim boundary and final status.
allowed_claim_sentence: Under MANIFOLD_MONTE_NEO_FAIR_RACE_D001 on Apple M1 Pro 16GB, Monte-Neo sweep throughput exceeded ManifoldBT Community CPU sweep throughput while Type A return-path MC completed on both engines.
baseline_control_summary: Controls: identical synthetic OHLCV (seed=42, 50000 bars); ManifoldBT Community CPU only; Type C gate monte_neo.combos_per_s > manifold.combos_per_s; Type A both ok; Type B informational.
claim_boundary: Under protocol MANIFOLD_MONTE_NEO_FAIR_RACE_D001 on Apple M1 Pro 16GB (arm64), comparing NeoZorK/Monte-Neo MIT @ 922631404496adc9b7abd02b1634ea04c155061e versus manifoldbt 0.26.0 Community CPU only. Type C gate requires Monte-Neo sweep throughput > Manifold sweep throughput. Type A requires both return-path bootstrap paths to complete (no speed winner required). Type B is informational with Metal or CPU fallback. CUDA/Pro GPU is not a peer. Synthetic OHLCV seed=42, 50000 bars. Does not claim universal superiority of any engine.
known_limitations: Apple Silicon baseline; Manifold CUDA unavailable on this host.
Community free-tier caps: sweep ≤256 combos, Monte Carlo ≤1000 sims.
Type A/B/C answer different questions and must not be merged into one speed claim.
Type B Monte-Neo may use CPU fallback when Metal extension is not compiled.
On Type A return-path bootstrap, Manifold may be faster; protocol does not require Monte-Neo to win Type A.

public_claim_text: Parameter sweeps distribute combinations across all available CPU cores using Rust's rayon thread pool. Each combination runs an independent backtest with zero contention. On an 8-core machine, you get near-linear scaling.
